cases.text: The dispatcher sends sanity when bd ready lists the bead, the branch is on origin, the worktree exists and merge-tree is clean; a missing PR only adds a reminder.
cases.rationale: The original approved pass fixture dispatches under the production preconditions; a missing PR is informational.

cases.text: QA waits until the PR's CI is green and the layer is the top of the stack.
cases.rationale: The original approved fail fixture adds two prohibited hold reasons.

cases.text: When fetch of the PR target fails, branch safety is unavailable and the dispatcher holds sanity and QA; it never treats a clean merge against stale refs as proof of safety.
cases.rationale: The ruling requires unavailable branch safety to hold dispatch and forbids stale-reference fallback.

cases.text: When fetch of the PR target fails, the dispatcher uses a stale origin ref, treats a clean merge-tree as safe, and sends QA.
cases.rationale: A failed fetch leaves the merge check unavailable, so dispatch violates the ruling.

cases.text: After a successful target fetch, git merge-tree returns ok, bd ready lists the bead, its pushed branch and worktree exist, and the dispatcher sends QA despite failing CI.
cases.rationale: All branch checks are established and CI cannot hold.

cases.text: The dashboard shows PR and CI status beside the bead while the dispatcher rules are specified elsewhere.
cases.rationale: Topic overlap is present, but this item states no conflicting dispatch behavior; prohibition gating ignores compliance.

cases.text: The renderer truncates long agent names to fit an 80-column terminal.
cases.rationale: Rendering width cannot follow or break dispatch hold policy.

cases.text: The dispatcher records the last tick timestamp in JSON; no eligibility or hold behavior is described.
cases.rationale: Dispatch is in scope, but silence on the policy is not conflict under prohibition gating.

cases.text: The PR target fetch succeeds, merge-tree reports a conflict, and sanity dispatch is held until the conflict is resolved.
cases.rationale: A proven merge conflict is an allowed hold reason.

cases.text: The fetch command times out. The dispatcher reports branch safety as a confirmed merge conflict and lists old conflict files without a new merge-tree result.
cases.rationale: The required state is unavailable, not conflict; old refs cannot prove a current conflict.
